北京时间 2026-11-28 的技术雷达

今天最重要的变化：推理系统不再只盯吞吐，而开始把低 token 数、低并发、beam search 等交互式路径视为首要优化对象。多个 PR 同时围绕 host 开销、小 batch kernel 融合与 CUDA graph 回放展开，这对 VLA 机器人上的小批量在线推理同样关键。

### 1. SGLang 为 beam search decode 增加 CUDA graph 回放

**原始材料**：[sgl-project/sglang#53659](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/53659)，2026-11-28（UTC），类型为开源 PR，来源 SGLang 仓库。

**解决旧问题**：在 `#44349` 引入 beam search 的共享上下文注意力与 trie 头之后，`DecodeCudaGraphRunner.can_run_graph` 对任何含 beam 输入的 decode batch 返回 False，导致这些 batch 只能 eager 启动每个 kernel，host launch 开销在低并发下主导延迟。

**技术机制**：新增 `BeamDecodeCudaGraphRunner` 子类，在平常 graph 旁额外 capture 一个读固定 buffer 的 beam graph；replay 前先将 beam 输入拷贝到固定 buffer。Trie 级别为每种 size 建图；共享上下文注意力只对 beam width 整数倍的 size 建图。默认共享上下文 kernel 的 decode 循环改为按运行时长度而非 `MAX_DECODE`，以便 eager 和 graph 编译相同 kernel、位级一致。提供 `SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_DECODE_GRAPH`、`SGLANG_BEAM_DECODE_GRAPH_FIXED_WIDTH`、`SGLANG_BEAM_DECODE_GRAPH_NEW_TOKEN_CAPACITY` 开关。

**与已有路线差别**：以往 CUDA graph 仅覆盖普通 decode，beam search 被完全排除；本 PR 通过专用 runner 与 hook 将 beam 纳入 graph 回放，同时保持 `_get_logits` 和基础 runner 不变。

**可信程度**：PR body 自述，提供准确性和速度测试；作者报告 900 requests/concurrency 下 beams 与 scores 位级相同，B300 上测试通过。但未核验代码合并与独立复现，CI 状态未确认。

**对机器人/VLA 及系统的启示**：beam search 常用于 LLM 规划器与搜索式解码；将其 decode 路径 GPU graph 化，可降低规划延迟波动，提升异步控制回路里“给机器人下一步指令”的确定性时间。VLA 若采用 beam search 输出动作 token，可能直接受益；可实验比较 beam graph vs eager 在真实 VLA planner 上的 TP99 与动作成功率。

### 2. SGLang 减少 beam search host sync，并加入 SM120 QuACK 与 split-KV

**原始材料**：[sgl-project/sglang#53660](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/53660)，2026-11-28（UTC），类型为开源 PR，来源 SGLang 仓库。

**解决旧问题**：在 SM120 上 256-beam 的 Qwen3-0.6B 请求 GPU 大部分时间空闲，等待 host sync、拷贝和 GC 暂停；SM120 还缺融合 gate_up GEMM，共享上下文 kernel 只填满少量 SM。

**技术机制**：默认开启四件事：beam-only batch 跳过 sampler（beam coordinator 直接选 token，capture 保留视图而非拷贝）；用 pinned memory 非阻塞拷贝上传 beam batch tail、trie level 和 coordinator 数据，使 overlap scheduler 在当前 step 执行时构建下一步；`BeamGroup.leader` 改弱引用，打破 `Req`-`BeamGroup` 循环，避免 GC 暂停；SM12x FA4 paged 调用按精确 shape 复用 host launch plan。可选：`SGLANG_USE_QUACK_SWIGLU_GEMM` 用 QuACK 在 epilogue 做 SiLU-and-mul，fp32 accumulator；`SGLANG_USE_BEAM_SHARED_CONTEXT_SPLIT_KV` 用 split-KV kernel 允许一个 captured graph 回放任意 prompt length。

**与已有路线差别**：不是增加新模型能力，而是消除 beam search 执行路径中的 host 屏障与冗余采样；split-KV 定位为 graph 回放专用，静态 shape。

**可信程度**：PR body 自述；默认路径位级相同于 main，作者报告 900 requests × 4 concurrency 100% 一致；split-KV 非位级相同，top-1 一致 93–97%。需注意这是开发者自测，不是独立评审。

**对机器人/VLA 及系统的启示**：异步控制要求 GPU 不等待 host 往返。此 PR 展示了如何通过非阻塞拷贝与跳过 sampler 降低 host 同步，直接对应 VLA 在线推理中“每步动作生成”的 host-GPU 耦合。机器人端若用独立规划进程，可参考其弱引用消除 GC 暂停的做法；可反证实验：在相同 beam search 负载下关闭 host sync 优化，测动作生成间隔的抖动是否显著增大。

### 3. SGLang disaggregation staging gather/scatter 矢量化

**原始材料**：[sgl-project/sglang#39236](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39236)，2026-11-27（UTC），类型为开源 PR，来源 SGLang 仓库。

**解决旧问题**：disaggregation 的 staging gather/scatter kernel 从 device pointer table 读 KV buffer 地址，Triton 无法推断对齐，导致标量 load/store；fused scatter 还占用 8KB shared memory。实际 KV buffer 16 字节对齐，但 kernel 不知道。

**技术机制**：给 gather/scatter kernel 增加 `ALIGNED_16` 特化，行基址加 `tl.multiple_of(..., 16)` hint，Triton 发出向量访问。Mooncake/NIXL 注册 KV buffer 时检查一次 `kv_buffers_preserve_16_byte_alignment` 并缓存；每次 transfer 只检查 staging buffer 地址（因其可能从 ring 任意 offset 开始）。不满足检查则回退 generic kernel。

**与已有路线差别**：利用运行时已知的对齐信息驱动编译期向量化，而不是默认保守标量化；对 scatter shared memory 从 8192 降到 0。

**可信程度**：PR body 提供基准：GB300 单 host 四 rank，gather kernel -6.5%，scatter kernel -30.9%，host-inclusive 相近且输出位级一致；H100 上 6 个测试通过，SM90/SM103 三元素大小共 36 组合编译验证。这些是作者自测，非端到端 RDMA 数据。

**对机器人/VLA 及系统的启示**：多机器人集中推理或跨节点 VLA 服务需要搬运 KV cache；gather/scatter 是异步传输的关键路径。矢量化 staging 降低的是 kernel 时间，RDMA 时间未变，因此整体收益依赖网络占比。对机器人场景，若多个机器人共享 context 并跨节点转移 KV，这项优化可降低切换延迟；可反证实验：在真实 RoCE 环境下测端到端 KV 迁移延迟，观察 scatter 优化是否被网络时间掩盖。

### 4. vLLM 集成 Mooncake EP all-to-all 后端

**原始材料**：[vllm-project/vllm#58375](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58375)，2026-11-27（UTC），类型为开源 PR，来源 vLLM 仓库。

**解决旧问题**：MoE 模型 expert-parallel 推理需要高效 all-to-all；vLLM 已有 DeepEP、NIXL-EP、MoonEP 等路径，但未集成 Mooncake EP，而 SGLang 已集成。

**技术机制**：增加 `mooncake_ep` A2A backend registry 条目、Mooncake EP CUDA communicator manager、`MooncakeEPPrepareAndFinalize`，并接入 modular `FusedMoEKernel` 路径。Mooncake 依赖保持可选，通过 package probe 检测。新增二 GPU 测试覆盖 dispatch/combine、reference local-expert、modular kernel、不同 token 数 BF16 输入。

**与已有路线差别**：直接复用 vLLM 现有的 EP 集成模式，不引入新抽象；主要是把成熟 backend 纳入统一 modular MoE 框架。

**可信程度**：PR body 自述；作者报告在 2 台 H20 上 PyTorch 2.13、Mooncake 0.3.13 下 6 个测试通过。尚未明确是否合并或大规模验证。

**对机器人/VLA 及系统的启示**：大规模 MoE VLA 模型在 multi-GPU 或多机器人服务器上运行时，all-to-all 通信决定 token 生成延迟。Mooncake EP 若提供更低 P50/P95 或更好的跨机带宽，可作为 VLA 分布推理的通信后端选择。但 PR 只验证 correctness，没有给出延迟/吞吐对比，因此不能推断性能优势。下一步值得在目标 MoE VLA 模型上 A/B 测试不同后端的高分位延迟。

### 5. vLLM 为 CUTLASS block-FP8 融合 SiLU-and-mul 与 group-128 FP8 量化

**原始材料**：[vllm-project/vllm#69778](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69778)，2026-11-28（UTC），类型为开源 PR，来源 vLLM 仓库。

**解决旧问题**：CUDA 上 `maybe_fused_act_quant` 的 `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` 从不触发；对于 block-FP8 checkpoint（如 Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 MoE FP8），每个 SiLU-and-mul 到 down_proj 边界需要两个 kernel（激活 + per_token_group_fp8_quant）。在 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 上每 decode step 有 40 个 shared-expert down_proj launch，在 1–16 token 时是关键路径。

**技术机制**：让 CUTLASS block-FP8 kernel 暴露 `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` 作为 input quant key，从而复用已有 fused producer；`Fp8LinearMethod` 对 block-quantized layers 暴露 `expose_input_quant_key`。关键改动：group-128 producer 改为写 column-major scales 匹配 kernel 读取布局。若 scale 行主序，GEMM 输出相对 RMS error 在 2 tokens 起达 46–71%。

**与已有路线差别**：不是新 kernel，而是让既有融合路径可达，并修正了 latent 的 scale layout 错误。

**可信程度**：PR body 提供配对实验：Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 TP1 B200，交换 GPU 抵消 node 差异，mean TPOT 改善 -3.8%/-2.5%/-2.4% at concurrency 1/4/8；GSM8K 精度与 main 无异。B300 独立重复结果相近。但仍是 PR 自测，未接受独立 review。

**对机器人/VLA 及系统的启示**：MoE VLA 在低 token 时共享专家是瓶颈，这类融合减少 kernel 数量，直接降低每步动作生成时间。更值得注意的是 scale layout 错误只在 >1 token 时暴露，提示低精度量化推理中布局一致性必须由测试覆盖；机器人端若对已量化模型做 kernel 变换，应增加多 token 的数值校验。可反证实验：在小 batch MoE VLA 上测 fused vs unfused 对动作成功率和 TPOT，并检查 scale layout 回归。

### 6. SGLang Inkling-2 在 SM120 上融合 block AttnRes、loop controller 与 RMSNorm

**原始材料**：[sgl-project/sglang#53299](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/53299)，2026-11-28（UTC），类型为开源 PR，来源 SGLang 仓库。

**解决旧问题**：Inkling-2-Mini 每个 step 执行 48 次 looped decoder visit，每次包含多个 block AttnRes 归约、loop controller 三阶段和 RMSNorm；在 SM120/SM121 上分开启动这些小 memory-bound kernel 带来大量 launch 和 HBM round-trip 开销。

**技术机制**：新增 SM12x-only CUDA JIT kernel：`attn_res_norm_bf16` 融合 block AttnRes 与 RMSNorm；`loop_pre_attn_rmsnorm` 用 3-stage producer/consumer PDL overlap 将 ctrl_down/ctrl_up/ctrl_merge_rmsnorm 融合。峰值 shared memory 控制在 8KB，满足 SM120 限制。运行时在 `inkling2.py` 接线，并保留地址别名以支持 captured graph。

**与已有路线差别**：针对循环式 decoder 架构（48 次 visit/step），不是常规 MoE/attention；通过 PDL overlap 掩盖生产者-消费者依赖。

**可信程度**：PR body 自述，包含精度 oracle 对比（候选 RMS error 不超过 baseline 1.02x）和微基准数据：SM120 上 pre-attn/MLP 融合在 local/global 场景下 1.3–3.3x 加速，SM121 小 L2 下收益下降。未核验完整模型端到端效果或模型质量。

**对机器人/VLA 及系统的启示**：如果 VLA 采取循环或状态空间式 token 混合，每 step 多次小归约会成为延迟瓶颈；使用融合与 PDL 能减少 launch。这提示具身模型若在 edge GPU 上运行，需按 SM 内存限制定制融合，而非照搬数据中心 kernel。可反证实验：在类似 looped decoder 的 VLA 模型上测试该策略是否改善动作频率，并评估模型输出是否因数值近似改变而影响成功率。

### 跨领域弱信号

今天多个 PR 同时聚焦“低并发、低 token、beam/规划路径”的 GPU 空闲与 host 同步问题。弱信号是：机器人 VLA 在线推理与 LLM 推理系统正收敛到同一批工程问题——kernel launch、host sync、CUDA graph、量化 layout。虽然这些 PR 都是软件系统优化，不改变模型能力，但它们会降低实际部署的尾部延迟。

### 趋势假设

1. **VLA 在线推理将采用 beam-search CUDA graph 与 host-sync 消除**（中等置信度）。可反证实验：在真实 VLA planner 上对比 graph replay 与 eager，测量动作成功率和 TP99 延迟；若延迟下降但成功率不变甚至下降，说明数值近似不可接受。

2. **MoE/FP8 推理中的小 batch 融合与 layout 修正会成为默认路线**（中等置信度）。可反证实验：在 Qwen 类 MoE 模型上关闭 fusion 并故意使用 row-major scale，看多 token 下精度是否严重劣化，验证 layout 修正的必要性。

3. **跨节点 KV 传输与 EP 后端的优化将推动多机器人集中式推理架构**（低置信度）。可反证实验：在两节点上同时跑 Mooncake EP、DeepEP、NIXL-EP 和矢量化 gather/scatter，比较 KV 迁移与 MoE token 生成的 P95/P99，看哪项成为实际瓶颈。

### 本周值得精读的 2 篇

1. [sgl-project/sglang#53659](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/53659)：Beam-search decode CUDA graph 回放，理解 beam 与 graph 的边界问题。
2. [vllm-project/vllm#69778](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69778)：FP8 SiLU-and-mul 融合与 scale layout 修正，关注数值一致性和小 batch 收益。

（注：以上均为 GitHub PR 描述与作者自测，未经同行评审；部分性能数据来自 PR body，未独立复现。所有链接为真实原始 URL。）

---
**本次采集**：共采集 301 条，去重后 301 条；候选池 120 条，本次精选 9 条。源异常 1 处（见仓库 Actions 日志）。

selected.summary: ## Motivation Mooncake provides an expert-parallel all-to-all communication backend for MoE models. This PR proposes integrating Mooncake EP into vLLM as an optional `mooncake_ep` A2A backend. Mooncake EP has already been integrated into SGLang. We would like to bring the backend to vLLM and discuss the appropriate evolution path with the vLLM community. ## Changes - Add `mooncake_ep` to the A2A backend registry. - Add the Mooncake EP CUDA communicator manager. - Add `MooncakeEPPrepareAndFinalize`. - Integrate Mooncake EP with the modular `FusedMoEKernel` path. - Add a two-GPU kernel/adapter correctness test covering: - Mooncake dispatch and combine; - reference local-expert execution; - modular `FusedMoEKernel` execution; - BF16 inputs with different token counts. The implementation follows the existing vLLM EP integration patterns used by DeepEP, NIXL-EP, and MoonEP. The Mooncake dependency remains optional and is detected through vLLM's package probe mechanism. ## Testing Tested on two H20 GPUs with: - PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 - Mooncake 0.3.13.post1 ```bash pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_mooncake_ep.py ``` Result: ```text 6 passed ``` We would be happy to work with the vLLM community on the evolution of this integration. Please let me know if there is any additional information, testing, or implementation change that would help with the review.

selected.title: [sgl-project/sglang PR] [Perf] beam-search: Replay all-beam decode batches as CUDA graphs
selected.summary: ## Motivation Follow-up to #44349. On main, `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.can_run_graph` returns False for any decode batch with beam inputs, so a batch that runs shared-context attention, the compact trie head, or both launches every kernel from the host. This PR replays those batches as CUDA graphs, from a beam-owned runner and behind an opt-in switch. The review of #44349 asked for graph replay as a follow-up under three conditions, and all three hold: 1. **Out of the shared runner.** The graph lives in a `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` subclass. The shared runner gains one hook (`_can_run_beam_graph`), and no `beam_trie` argument, key type, `type(self)` gate or `getattr`. 2. **`_get_logits` as on main.** It is untouched. 3. **Benchmarked on its own.** See Speed Tests. The change is ported from the author's fork PR (lauthu/sglang#12), and the commit keeps Xinyu Liu as its author. ## Modifications - **`BeamDecodeCudaGraphRunner`** (`srt/beam_search/beam_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`, new): next to the ordinary graph of each decode graph size, it captures a beam graph that reads the beam inputs from fixed buffers, and a replay copies the batch into them first. - Trie levels: every size gets a graph; the batch pads like any decode batch. - Shared-context attention: only sizes that are a multiple of the beam width get a graph, and a batch needs exactly such a size. Every request must have the configured beam width and fit the decode capacity. - A batch that fits no beam graph runs eagerly as on main; a batch mixing beam and regular requests, or a server with neither fast path on, takes the ordinary path. - **One hook** in `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: `can_run_graph` asks `_can_run_beam_graph` for a beam batch; the base returns False, so the base runner is unchanged. - **Runner selection** in `model_runner.py`: `BeamDecodeCudaGraphRunner.enabled()` is true when the switch is on, with no speculative decoding, no pipeline parallelism and no DP attention (beam requests are refused under the last three). - **Default shared-context kernel**: its decode loop runs over the runtime decode length instead of a `MAX_DECODE` constexpr. Eager and graph now compile the same kernel and give bit-identical outputs. - **Env vars** (also in the environment variable reference): - `SGLANG_ENABLE_BEAM_DECODE_GRAPH` (default off) - `SGLANG_BEAM_DECODE_GRAPH_FIXED_WIDTH`: the requests' beam width under shared-context attention; without it those batches get no graph. - `SGLANG_BEAM_DECODE_GRAPH_NEW_TOKEN_CAPACITY`: on a model without a trie, the tokens a graph holds per request; it is the graph's capacity, not a limit on requests. - **Tests**: unit tests for the buffer loading, the replay gate and the capture config; a GPU test that replays graphs of two sizes against the eager kernel; `test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_parity.py` gains a graph class that also checks a beam request replays a graph. With shared-context attention, `--cuda-graph-bs-decode` counts rows, so it lists `beam width * k` for each number `k` of requests that may decode together. ## Accuracy Tests - Graph vs eager over 900 requests per concurrency: beams and scores are bit-identical. - Before the kernel loop change they differed by about 1 bf16 ulp in the kernel (top-1 equal for 99.0-99.7%), because eager and graph compiled different unrolls. - `test/manual/beam_search/test_beam_parity.py` (all classes) passes on B300 with `--attention-backend flashinfer --page-size 1`. - Unit tests pass. ## Speed Tests and Profiling B300, one GPU. Qwen3-0.6B copy with a 1,000,000-item trie; 2,048-token prompts; 256 beams; 3 new tokens; shared-context attention on. 3 rounds rotated; mean latency by requests in flight (`c`). | Arm | c = 1 (ms) | c = 2 (ms) | c = 4 (ms) | c = 8 (ms) | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---:

selected.title: [sgl-project/sglang PR] [Perf] disaggregation: Vectorize staging gather/scatter for aligned KV buffers
selected.summary: ## Motivation The staging gather/scatter kernels read KV buffer addresses from a pointer table on the device. Triton cannot infer alignment from a loaded pointer, so the KV side is lowered to scalar loads and stores. In the PTX for the current kernels, the payload moves one element at a time, and the fused scatter kernel also uses 8 KB of shared memory that the vectorized version does not need. The KV buffers are 16-byte aligned in practice. The kernel just has no way to know. ## Modifications - Add an `ALIGNED_16` specialization to the gather and scatter kernels. When it is on, the row bases get a `tl.multiple_of(..., 16)` hint and Triton emits vector loads and stores. For scatter, the hint covers the fused and persistent kernels; the per-page scatter kernel keeps generic addressing. - Check the KV buffers once when Mooncake or NIXL registers them (`kv_buffers_preserve_16_byte_alignment`, called from `build_staging_kv_buffer_info`). The result is stored with the buffer info, so transfers do not rescan the buffer list. - On each transfer, only the staging buffer address is checked (`_can_use_aligned_staging_copy`), because it can start at any ring offset. The strides and head offsets come from the buffer shape, so the registration check covers them. If any check fails, the transfer uses the generic kernel, same as today. Nothing changes when staging is disabled, and nothing changes for buffers that fail the checks. ## Test New test file: `test/registered/kernels/ops/kvcache/test_disaggregation_staging_buffer.py` - Gather and scatter give bit-exact results on both the aligned path and the generic path, for 1, 2, and 4-byte element sizes. - Misaligned KV buffers, a misaligned staging offset, and an odd head size stay on the generic path and are still bit-exact. Ran the test file on an H100 with torch 2.14.1 and Triton 3.8.0: all 6 tests pass. Compiled both kernels offline with Triton 3.8.0 for SM90 and SM103 and all three element sizes, 36 combinations in total. The generic version generates the same PTX as upstream. The aligned version uses vector accesses, and scatter shared memory goes from 8192 to 0 bytes. ## Benchmark Measured on GB300 (one host, four ranks): BF16, 80 layers, 1024 tokens from a 4096-token pool, page size 1, 8 KV heads with head dim 128, prefill TP4 to decode TP1. Baseline and aligned use the same inputs, grids, and warmups. Only `ALIGNED_16` differs. "Kernel" is CUDA graph replay. "Host-inclusive" adds the per-transfer alignment check to the candidate side. selected.summary: ## Overview `maybe_fused_act_quant` already has a fused SiLU-and-mul + dynamic group-128 FP8 producer (`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant`, registered for `(SiluAndMul, kFp8Dynamic128Sym)`). On CUDA it never fires: no linear kernel reports `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` from `input_quant_key()`, so `get_input_quant_key()` is always `None` and the down projection quantizes its own input. For block-FP8 checkpoints that use `quant_method: fp8` (for example the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 MoE FP8 releases), every SiLU-and-mul → `down_proj` boundary therefore runs two kernels, the activation and `per_token_group_fp8_quant`. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 that is the 40 shared-expert `down_proj` launches per decode step. The shared expert runs on the aux stream at decode, but at 1–16 tokens it is the longer of the two branches, so its kernels are on the critical path. This PR makes the existing fusion reachable for the CUTLASS block-FP8 kernel: 1. `CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.input_quant_key()` returns `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` when that is the layer's activation key and the kernel pads no tokens. 2. `Fp8BlockScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights` accepts a `QuantizedActivation` and skips its own input quant. 3. `Fp8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading` calls `expose_input_quant_key` for block-quantized layers. This method never exposed a key before; the modelopt, online-FP8, compressed-tensors and Quark methods already do. Per-tensor and per-channel `fp8` layers are left as they are. 4. The group-128 producer writes **column-major** scales, which is the layout this kernel reads (its own `QuantFP8` uses `column_major_scales=True`). Item 4 is required, not cosmetic. The producer wrote row-major scales, which only coincide with column-major at one token. Today nothing consumes them, so this was latent. At startup the engine checks the decoder exposed by `language_model`. This path requires a `DecoderModelForCausalLM` and one pipeline stage. - **Eager fallback:** Calls with different layouts, nested structures, shapes, dtypes, or host values run eagerly. selected.summary: ## Description On an 8-GPU Kimi K3.1 generation server, every MoE layer ends with the fused latent-MoE tail (`modules/kimi_k3_moe_tail`). After the routed experts' second GEMM (TRTLLM-Gen FC2) it runs two kernels: - the collective: top-16 weighted sum of this rank's FC2 rows, all-reduce of the latent rows over the 8 ranks with the RMSNorm, and a reduce-scatter of the shared-expert partials; - the up-projection: this rank's 896 of the 7168 output columns, plus the shared shard, stored through the multicast mapping of the tail's mailbox (the all-gather), where the next layer's mix reads it. For steps of up to 8 tokens this PR runs one kernel instead of those two (`wave_tail.py`). It is adapted from the one-group path of vLLM's `WaveMoeTail` (Apache-2.0, credited in the file header): - One launch of 112 CTAs (seven 16-CTA clusters, one CTA per SM). At entry every thread loads its fragment of the rank's up-projection shard into registers, which overlaps the routed experts. - After the wait on FC2, cluster 0 does the top-16 weighted sum and multicasts this rank's latent fragment; the other clusters store the shared-expert shards to their owner ranks. - Every cluster polls the eight ranks' latent fragments (an unpublished chunk holds a sentinel), sums them in rank order, normalizes, and runs the up-projection as BF16 `mma.sync` chains against the weights it already holds. The owner CTA of each output line adds the shared shard and multicasts the line into the same mailbox the two kernels write. **Differences from vLLM's kernel** - It does the top-16 weighted sum itself, after the experts finish. vLLM's routed experts publish the latent rows from their own epilogue; TRTLLM-Gen's FC2 is precompiled, so that part is not possible here. - It releases its dependents (the next layer's mix) only after its own wait, as the existing tail kernels do. - It keeps its three-slot buffer rotation on the device: a small `state` tensor holds the slot and row count of the previous launch, and each launch re-arms that slot after its own output is out. The host passes nothing that depends on the call sequence, so CUDA graphs replay it. **When it runs.** `fused_tail_wave_requested`: 8 ranks, the 7168 x 3584 shape, the finalize fold on (the default), and `KIMI_K3_FUSED_MOE_TAIL_WAVE=1`; with the variable unset it is on for SM103 (GB300), where it was measured. `KIMI_K3_FUSED_MOE_TAIL_WAVE=0` turns it off. The kernel is optional: if a rank cannot build it, every rank drops it (one more collective check at construction) and the two kernels serve those steps as before. The model code is unchanged; the choice is made inside the tail op. With DSpark draft length 5 a step verifies 6 tokens per request, so this covers one request per step; without speculative decoding it covers up to 8 requests. More than 8 tokens keep the two kernels: I tried vLLM's way of handling them (an all-reduce into a local buffer that every cluster then reads) and polling the sources directly, and neither was clearly faster than the two kernels on GB300. **Shared helper.** `finalize_top16_bf16` (the top-16 weighted sum the collective already uses) gets a `side_effects` option, off by default. The new kernel does work in front of its grid-dependency wait, so the loads of the FC2 rows must not be moved in front of it. **Numerics.** Those of the two kernels (rank-order FP32 sum of the routed fragments, one BF16 rounding, BF16-rounded squares, up-projection rounded to BF16 before the BF16 shared shard is added in FP32), except for the summation order of the sum of squares and of the up-projection. On the unit test's random inputs for 1 to 8 tokens, 750 of 2,064,384 output numbers (0.036%) differ from the two kernels, by at most 0.031. Both are equally close to the FP32 reference: mean absolute

selected.summary: ## Overview Add an SM100-family `tcgen05` CUDA kernel that fuses the Qwen4Exp hyperconnection down projection, the injection columns, and SiLU in one launch. It takes over from the `Linear` → split → `hc_silu` chain for eligible merged weights at `M > 48`; the CuTeDSL kernel from [#58957](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58957) still handles `M 48` only. **E2E perf** `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, MTP3 speculative decoding, FP8 KV cache + FP8 indexer cache, prefix caching off, `vllm bench serve` with 8192-token inputs and 1024-token outputs. TEP4 (TP4 + expert parallel, 4x B300), both arms on the same node: | concurrency | base tok/s | PR tok/s | Δ | base TPOT | PR TPOT | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 356.4 | 368.7 | +3.4% | 2.70 | 2.61 | | 4 | 973.0 | 1003.6 | +3.1% | 3.87 | 3.80 | | 16 | 2379.5 | 2427.4 | +2.0% | 6.32 | 6.18 | | 64 | 4513.7 | 4680.0 | +3.7% | 13.41 | 12.94 | - With EP the MoE layers are cheaper, so the HC chain takes a larger share of decode time and the kernel's gain is most visible here. - TP1 (one B300, three interleaved rounds): +0.7–2.5% at concurrency 16–64, ~0% at 1–4 where decode batches sit below the `M > 48` cutoff (c64 TPOT 24.91 → 24.71 ms in the same-node round). One further round was discarded: a faulty node in the pool ran both arms 2–4x slower, including at concurrency 1 where this kernel is inactive. **E2E accuracy** TP1, MTP3, FP8 KV + FP8 indexer cache, prefix caching on, greedy GSM8K (5-shot, 2 epochs, 1319 problems): | arm | strict-match | flexible-extract | |---|---:|---:| | base | 0.9693 | 0.9685 | | PR | 0.9708 | 0.9701 | The +0.2pp delta is within run-to-run eval noise. ## Details - The kernel runs a `tcgen05` GEMM with the injection columns in the same projection and a fused SiLU epilogue. A cost model over `(M, sm_count)` selects among eight configurations in three families: one-wave 1-SM Push-DSMEM split-K for decode, 2-SM Push-DSMEM split-K at intermediate `M`, and persistent 2-SM for prefill. - With PDL, the `w_down` producer can start loading the static weight before the dependency resolves; the `xn` producer waits for the preceding kernel. The op docstring records the static-weight contract. - The epilogue applies SiLU directly to the fp32 `tcgen05` accumulator values and rounds the result to bf16, while the unfused path rounds the GEMM output to bf16 before SiLU.
